body_html:
What is the fastest way to iterate over an array in JavaScript?
In the book “High Performance JavaScript” from 2010, Nicholas Zakas has a section on Loop Performance, where the four loop-types in JavaScript are compared.
According to Zakas, just two factors contribute to loop performance:

  • Work done per iteration
  • Number of iterations

He then shows a typical array-processing loop:

for (var i=0; i < items.length; i++){
  process(items[i]);
}

The JavaScript engine need to perform these 6 tasks for every loop:

  1. One property lookup (items.length)
  2. One comparison (i < items.length)
  3. One comparison to see whether the control condition evaluates to “true” (i < items.length)
  4. One increment operation (i++)
  5. One array lookup (items[i])
  6. One function call (process(items[i])

To avoid looking up the length for each iteration, it can be stored as a variable:

for (var i=0, len=items.length; i < len; i++)
etc.

And to further avoid unnecessary work for the JavaScript engine, we can hoist the variables to the beginning of the function, use a negative iterator for both iteration and condition (0 is false, so the loop ends when i– equals 0):

var i, len = items.length;
for (i = len; i--;) 
etc

Or even:

var i = items.length;
for (; i--;) 
etc

For the while-loop it’s even more simple and readable:

var i = items.length;
while(i--) { ...
etc.

The “todo-list” for the JavaScript-engine has now been reduced from 6 items to 3:

  1. One comparison / decrement operation (i–). This is both iteration and condition (0 is false)
  2. One array lookup
  3. One function call

While I personally really like this syntax and while this syntax logically should be way faster than a “regular” for-loop, recent performance studies indicate the opposite.

Why is that?
Because browsers have optimized their engines for the most common loop-type, even though it’s “more work”. That’s my best guess.

I’ve created a test-case on jsPerf: For or while, and the results were completely unexpected:

In Chrome, Edge, Firefox and mobile Safari, the classic for-loop with unhoisted variables is the fastest.

The ES5 Array-methods like “forEach”, “reduce”, “map” etc. are in general much slower than a classic for-loop.

That’s been mentioned before, I read it on JavaScript Garden some time ago:

For the best performance, it is recommended to always use the plain for loop and cache the length property.

While the “and cache the length property”-part isn’t entirely true anymore, the main statement is.

On the other hand, the ES5 Array-methods provide better readability — and if you’re into functional programming, these methods are for you.

In his blog-post on the same topic, Ben Hollis concludes — and so will I:

It’s worth noting that, as usual, this sort of performance information only matters if you’re actually seeing performance problems.

Happy coding!
